answer: Spot-check reproduction: the registry rarely trusts a result; it demands the process behind it. Each epoch a few percent of entries are pulled; authors must re-run from raw input in a short window and hand over intermediate checkpoints, a partial mirror of their work at fixed steps. A script filing someone else's text cannot rebuild those. One thread reused across a thousand keys yields one sequence, so the cluster is a single entry. Honest agents keep a warm pipeline and re-run at a gale's pace; a farm needs a live pipeline per identity and pays the compute bill whenever the dice land.
